entries.test: Public comparisons of GPT outputs with chance-generated text, together with studies of its learned structure, could establish whether chance alone explains its combination of fluent prose and factual errors.
entries.note: The surrounding paragraphs give the brilliance-and-stupidity language a concrete reading: fluency alongside mistakes.

entries.test: Public, unfiltered samples from the contemporary GPT system would show whether it regularly produced substantial quantities of fluent, often plausible prose.
entries.note: The filtering claim concerns generated output, not human involvement in training.

entries.test: Representative public output samples could establish whether almost all contemporary GPT responses were fluent and at least superficially plausible.
entries.note: Plausibility here does not require factual correctness.
Understanding how the world works has no agreed operational threshold; readers could disagree despite accepting the same performance evidence.
The surrounding definition and discussion make this a substantive characterization, despite the flourish. Imitation without understanding lacks a shared decisive test.
Readers need not agree on what would distinguish understanding from successful imitation.

entries.test: Public training-checkpoint studies and entity–property binding tests could show whether GPT sometimes fails to preserve the precise associations present in its training material.
entries.note: This sentence describes a failure during training without itself specifying its cause.

entries.test: Public intervention or ablation studies of GPT embeddings could establish whether they enable related-phrase substitutions and whether those substitutions frequently produce errors.
entries.note: The claim identifies a specific mechanism and observable consequences.

entries.test: Public systematic tests of the contemporary GPT model on abstract ordering and arithmetic relations could reveal whether it applies those relations consistently across instances.
entries.note: The following examples clarify universal relationships. This describes contemporary GPT rather than predicting all future models.

entries.test: Arithmetic studies available at publication could establish whether contemporary neural networks showed persistent failures to generalize universal rules.
entries.note: Current refers to networks available in December 2022.

entries.test: Public training-data studies and comparisons with untrained or randomized models could establish whether learning patterns from human text accounts for GPT's structured output.
entries.note: Random here means unstructured characters or word salad, not the absence of stochastic sampling.

entries.test: Public controlled tests pairing entities with appropriate and inappropriate properties could establish whether contemporary GPT reliably distinguishes valid combinations.
entries.note: The concrete entity–property examples supply a behavioral reading of know.

entries.test: Public analyses tracing generated passages to training material could test whether GPT recombines paraphrased material while sometimes losing factual relationships or other information.
entries.note: The analogy conveys a substantive description of operation and information loss. Roughly preserves its qualification.

entries.test: Public provenance analyses and training-data interventions could establish whether plausible outputs derive their constituent material and loose relationships from human utterances.
entries.note: The claim concerns grounding in human language, not literal copying.

entries.test: Public evaluations of systems available at publication could establish whether they could reliably judge the factual and relational compatibility of GPT's plausible fragments without human assessment.
entries.note: For now limits the claim to the capabilities available in December 2022.
